name: Brute force response
description:
A first-responder checklist for a credential-guessing incident: establish whether anything succeeded before deciding how urgent this is, then contain and follow up.
Note the two steps carrying `intended_*` fields. Those name an action rather than binding to a catalog entry, and they will import as ordinary manual tasks on your deployment — wire them to your own automation deliberately, which is also the moment to think about whether that response should be allowed to run unattended.

name: FortiGate Firewall Login Outside Office Hours
description: This rule detects logins to a fortigate firewall outside normal office hours.

name: Multiple failed logins followed by a succes full login on vaultwarden.
description:
Alerts triggers when multiple failed logins are followed by a successfull login to vaultwarden from the same source ip address.
Requires vaultwarden logging, successfull 100201 and failed 100202.

name: SSH brute force from a single source
description:
Repeated failed SSH authentication from one source address within a short window — the classic credential-guessing shape. Built entirely on stock Wazuh sshd rule ids (5710 "attempt to login using a non-existent user" and 5716 "authentication failed"), so it is portable to any deployment running the default ruleset with no local rules required.
Tune `count` to your estate before enabling: 20 in 15 minutes is deliberately conservative and will stay quiet on most networks. A perimeter host exposed to the internet will see this constantly from background noise, which is why the Backtest number matters more than the default.
